definitionOfDone: All seven plug styles remain instantly distinguishable by their terminal assembly while sharing one cleaner SAKURA construction language.
Every style remains inside the current 0.18 radius and 0.64 length envelope in front, side and three-quarter views.
Cable corners use tangent low-poly fillets without Catmull-Rom overshoot, spherical elbow bulges, gaps or reversed short-segment bends.
Static, double-ended, showcase and appliance-flight cables share the same section, material hierarchy and plug attachment.
Hover, blocked, energized, picking, reset, disposal and progressive extraction behavior remain compatible with existing callers.

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: PLUG_HEAD_ENVELOPE and puzzle collision constants are authoritative.
The isolated round-two-pin image establishes the common family proportion, while the seven-style board establishes identity.
SAKURA city screenshots are style-only evidence and do not override plug dimensions.
All dynamic path mutations remain owned by existing gameplay systems; the new helpers are rendering-only.

featureReviews.notes: The old straight cylinder and spherical end bulges are replaced by a readable twelve-facet five-stage shell, restrained shoulder, and stepped strain relief while preserving the family proportions.

visualEvidence.notes: Left is archived v1; right is v2 blockout. Different capture scale does not affect silhouette review.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: The v2 silhouette has a clearer rear-neck/body/front-shoulder hierarchy and controlled planar facets. It avoids bulbous toy rounding. Terminal details are intentionally unchanged in this pass.

featureReviews.notes: All seven layouts retain their defining count, spacing, cavity, and front-face cues; the new dark interface ring improves separation from the shared shell.
The cable, terminal, and indicator sockets are explicit zero-triangle nodes; every visible assembly part has a stable semantic name and destruction group.

visualEvidence.notes: The board verifies every PlugStyleId at the same scale and light; runtime sockets and groups are code-verified.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: The dark faceplate ring makes the terminal assembly read as a real inserted component instead of pins floating from one cylinder. The stepped rear and recessed side indicator remain restrained and inside the family silhouette.

featureReviews.notes: The refined shell reads clearly at gameplay scale and keeps the plug identity without the old straight-cylinder silhouette.
Round pins, blades, three-pin clusters, barrel cavity, USB-C face, grounding layout and pogo contacts remain distinct in the family and gameplay views.
The fixed-seed game view shows controlled low-poly quarter turns without the v1 spherical elbow bulges; analytic tests confirm tangent continuity and bounded centerlines.

visualEvidence.notes: Code tests supply the tangent and no-overshoot evidence that cannot be read exactly from the dense gameplay image.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: The new corners maintain the original orthogonal corridors but replace hard sphere-jointed elbows with compact faceted turns. Dense overlaps stay legible, and plug-to-cable joints remain continuous at gameplay scale.

featureReviews.notes: Shell, shoulder, rubber relief, dark cavity, cool gray-violet terminals and recessed indicator now form a controlled SAKURA palette with broad three-step facet shading.

visualEvidence.notes: The material split is visible across seven shell colors under one neutral rig.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: The broad planar highlights align with the SAKURA city props and avoid photographic roughness noise. The darker connector face and rubber transitions improve construction readability without mechanical panel clutter.

featureReviews.notes: Front, three-quarter, and side views show restrained deep-purple silhouette ink, readable planar highlights, shallow relief rings, and a layered status inset without glossy or noisy surface treatment.

visualEvidence.notes: Three fixed views were captured at one orthographic scale; side view exposes the inset status layer and facet response.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: The front and side captures reveal broad planar highlight changes instead of smooth plastic rolls. Outline weight remains on macro construction edges and avoids doubling tiny terminal details.

featureReviews.notes: Warm key, cool fill, soft blossom rim and the production renderer's explicit NoToneMapping preserve the game's saturated SAKURA palette without shadow acne or photoreal reflections.

visualEvidence.notes: Accepted image is the post-refinement render with no self-shadow striping.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: A rejected intermediate ACES/self-shadow variant introduced muted colors and shadow acne; the accepted render restores the production palette and clean toon bands while retaining a subtle rear rim.

featureReviews.notes: The exploded debug capture proves seven selectable semantic parts per head, and the successful raycast selection is published through diagnostics while sockets, colliders, and destruction groups remain available in sculptRuntime.

proceduralStrategy: Use a twelve-segment LatheGeometry profile for the shared shell and strain relief.

Build orthogonal cable paths from line segments and analytic quarter-circle Curve segments; never use free Catmull-Rom smoothing.

Publish nodes, sockets, pick groups and destruction groups through root.userData.sculptRuntime.
